section_summary: This section centers on Far East Photo Review’s request for permission to circulate its magazine in occupied Japan: State Department officials directed the publisher to the War Department’s Reorientation Branch while privately judging the publication unsuitable for reorientation work. Most of the section is the enclosed March 1947 issue, featuring extensive coverage of the 1946 Nankai earthquake, repatriation, Japanese economic and cultural life, diaspora communities, and commercial advertising. The section concludes with a 1948 airgram reporting Japanese criticism of inconsistent Occupation press censorship and a fragmentary 1947 airgram routing sheet.

subfiles.title: Letter advising George Goodstadt how to seek permission to circulate Far East Photo Review in Japan
subfiles.from: Edwin M. Martin, Chief, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs
subfiles.to: George Goodstadt, Agent, Far East Photo Review
subfiles.about: Martin directs Goodstadt to the War Department office responsible for approving material for circulation in occupied Japan.
subfiles.summary: Martin tells George Goodstadt to apply to the War Department's Reorientation Branch at 292 Madison Avenue, New York, which decides what circulates in Japan.

subfiles.title: Memorandum concerning circulation of Far East Photo Review in Japan
subfiles.about: Schuler recommends referring the applicant to the Reorientation Branch while privately describing the magazine as unsuitable for Japanese reorientation.
subfiles.summary: Schuler advises giving the inquirer the Reorientation Branch address and privately judges Far East Photo Review highly unsuitable for encouraging Japanese American irredentism rather than syncretism.

subfiles.title: Request for authorization to distribute Far East Photo Review in Japan
subfiles.from: George Goodstadt, Agent, Far East Photo Review
subfiles.to: Edwin M. Martin, Chief, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs
subfiles.about: Goodstadt asks how to obtain State Department clearance to distribute the magazine among occupation personnel and the Japanese public.
subfiles.summary: Goodstadt encloses Far East Photo Review, read by people of Japanese origin across the Americas, saying it explains democratization under MacArthur; told State clearance was needed, he asks for instructions.

subfiles.title: Far East Photo Review, March 1947, No. 2
subfiles.about: The illustrated bilingual magazine presents news, features, cultural material, and advertising concerning postwar Japan and overseas Japanese communities.
subfiles.summary: The issue’s principal illustrated feature documents the December 1946 Nankai earthquake and tsunami, including destruction in Wakayama, Shingu, Tanabe, Kushimoto, Kainan, Awaji, and neighboring districts, scientific discussion of earthquake prediction, relief work, casualties, and reconstruction costs. Other articles cover the repatriation of Japanese prisoners and civilians, inflation and production, overseas trade, lacquerware, judo and other sports, penicillin research, film and theater, radio democratization programs, Japanese American relief activities, restaurants, businesses, and community entertainment. Numerous advertisements and profiles link Japanese recovery with Japanese American commercial and cultural networks in New York and Chicago.

subfiles.title: Airgram A-69 reporting Kazuo Kawai’s criticism of Occupation press censorship
subfiles.about: The airgram summarizes an off-the-record talk by Nippon Times editor Kazuo Kawai about censorship of the Japanese press under the Occupation.
subfiles.summary: Airgram A-69: Kazuo Kawai says GHQ censorship favors positive reporting on the Soviet Union and suppresses criticism of an Allied power, citing deletions from Louis Fischer and Lippmann; inexperienced censors make it erratic, and papers found indirect signals.

subfiles.title: Incoming airgram routing sheet fragment
subfiles.about: The page is a fragmentary Department of State incoming-airgram routing and action sheet without the substantive message text.
subfiles.summary: Incoming airgram routing sheet fragment dated March 18, 1947; sender and message not legible.
